editorial:
If you love buddy cop movies but want something that pokes fun at the whole genre, this one is a blast. Will Ferrell plays a desk-loving detective who would rather do paperwork than chase bad guys, while Mark Wahlberg is his angry partner who desperately wants to be a hero. Their chemistry is the real star here, with Ferrell's deadpan awkwardness bouncing perfectly off Wahlberg's loud frustration. The movie opens with a hilarious scene featuring two superstar cops who get taken out in the most ridiculous way possible, setting the tone for everything that follows. The jokes come fast, the action is surprisingly solid, and there are plenty of quotable lines you will be repeating for days.

The pacing rarely slows down, though some of the financial crime plot gets a little confusing if you are not paying close attention. The supporting cast is packed with funny faces, and the action scenes are bigger than you might expect from a comedy. It is not perfect, since a few gags run a bit long, but the laughs far outweigh the misses. If you want a fun movie night with friends, this is a great pick. endingExplained: In the final act, Gamble and Hoitz uncover a massive financial fraud scheme run by a wealthy businessman who has been stealing billions through a Ponzi-like operation. After a chaotic shootout and chase, the two cops finally get their moment of glory and arrest the villain. The twist is that instead of getting celebrated like the heroic cops from the opening, they are mostly ignored by the media and their department. The movie ends with a funny credits sequence showing real financial crime statistics, reminding you that the real bad guys often get away with it.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves buddy cop comedies and Will Ferrell movies.
